overall_summary: Space-themed shorts, particularly those focusing on extreme exoplanet conditions, paradoxical physics, and bizarre cosmic weather, are the clear drivers of growth for FACTVERSE. Conversely, over-saturated psychology and brain trivia topics consistently underperform, failing to capture viewer attention in the first few seconds.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' achieved 1,055 views, and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' secured 963 views and 34 likes, showing the highest engagement on the channel.
winning_patterns.action: Focus content production on bizarre cosmic anomalies, extreme planetary climates, and mind-bending space phenomena with highly visual, sensory-rich hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' generated only 5 to 53 views, and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize generic psychological facts. If psychology is covered, it must be framed through a cinematic, high-stakes micro-story rather than dry trivia.

next_video.concept: The Egg-Shaped Planet Being Eaten Alive (WASP-12b)
next_video.opening_direction: Show a realistic CGI render of a distorted, egg-shaped planet being stretched apart by a massive star with the hook: 'This planet is shaped like an egg because its own star is literally eating it alive.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet is being devoured so rapidly that it loses 189 quadrillion tons of mass every year, meaning it will completely vanish in a cosmic blink of an eye.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven success of extreme exoplanet conditions while utilizing a highly shocking visual hook (egg-shaped planet) and high-stakes cosmic destruction.

experiment: Test a cinematic 'What-If' space disaster scenario, such as 'What If Earth Was Sucked Into a Wandering Rogue Planet?', to see if combining extreme space physics with catastrophic survival storytelling increases viewer retention.
